subject: maths
title: Perimeter & Area of Polygons
welcome_lead: Measure around shapes and inside them. Perimeter and area are the foundation of geometry.
meta_desc: Master perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms in this KS3 adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! You can measure shapes inside and out.

concepts.def: The total distance around the outside of a shape.
The amount of surface a 2D shape covers.
A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.
The bottom side used to measure area.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area = length × width.

For a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm: Area = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) = 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

Area = ½ × base × height.

For a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm: Area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

Area = base × perpendicular height.

For base 7 cm and height 4 cm: Area = 7 × 4 = 28 cm².

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).
Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
They add up to 180 degrees.

mcqs.q: Can Pythagoras' theorem be used on any triangle?
options: Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
No — it only applies to right-angled triangles.
Yes — it works on any triangle as long as you square the sides.
